newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian shipper says wins $35.5 mln foreign loan.
newsitem.headline: Croatian shipper says wins $35.5 mln foreign loan.

text.p: Croatian shipper Atlantska Plovidba has signed a deal for a $35.5 million loan with Germany's Hamburgische Landesbank, the company said in a statement.

The eight-year loan is repayable at 1.20 percent over Libor, it said in a news release faxed to Reuters. The loan was signed on Wednesday in the Adriatic port and scenic tourist resort of Dubrovnik, where Atlantska is based.
"The loan funds will be used to refinance $14.5 million in outstanding liabilities and $21 million to buy newer second-hand vessels," it said.
Atlantska has invested some $50 million in the renewal of its fleet over the past two years. It currently operates 20 vessels, of which 17 are used for long haul journeys.
The company also plans to invest 10 million German marks in reconstruction of Dubrovnik's Grand Hotel Imperijal, the statement said.
"With this investment, Atlantska Plovidba will become majority owner of the hotel, controlling a 65 percent stake," it said.
Some 60.5 percent of the company's 136.2 million German mark equity is in private hands and the rest is controlled by the state privatisation agency.
Its shareholders recently approved a dividend payout of 3.50 kuna per share on its 1996 net profit of $278,300. Figures for 1995 were not available.
Atlantska's shares, traded in a segment for semi-regulated firms, closed last week at 160 kuna on Zagreb's bourse.
